findings.description: RES-4 uses bare negated commands as assertions: `! grep -q 'claude-opus-4-7' .../hitl-jury-panel/SKILL.md` and `! grep -q 'claude-3-5-sonnet' .../alternative-model.md`. Under bats-core, test bodies run with `set -eET` plus an ERR trap, and bash exempts `!`-inverted commands from both errexit and the ERR trap. Neither line is the final command of the test, so a non-zero result from `! grep` is simply discarded. This is the documented bats gotcha ("My negated statement does not fail the test"), which is why bats 1.5.0 added `run !`. The two residue checks therefore can never go red, even though RES-4 is cited as G-4 acceptance evidence for AC 1 (no previous-generation pins in hitl-jury-panel or the persona).
findings.failure_mode: If `claude-opus-4-7` is reintroduced into hitl-jury-panel/SKILL.md, or `claude-3-5-sonnet` into alternative-model.md, RES-4 still passes 7/7 and the residue gate reports clean. The 'red first' claim for this test cannot hold for these two assertions because they are unconditionally true.
findings.suggested_fix: Add `bats_require_minimum_version 1.5.0` to setup() and rewrite as `run ! grep -q 'claude-opus-4-7' "$R/.claude/skills/hitl-jury-panel/SKILL.md"` and `run ! grep -q 'claude-3-5-sonnet' "$R/.claude/data/personas/alternative-model.md"`. Alternatively use the pattern already used in RES-6: `run grep -q ...; [ "$status" -eq 1 ]`. Verify the fix goes red by temporarily inserting the forbidden string.

findings.description: RES-1 pins claude-opus-5-5 pricing as input 4000000, output 20000000, cache_read 200000 (micro-dollars per MTok, i.e. $4 / $20 / $0.20). Anthropic's published prompt-caching price structure prices cache reads at 0.1x the base input rate, which for a $4 input price would be $0.40 = 400000. The pinned value is a 0.05x ratio. The implementation report says the entry is 'vendor-sourced' for input/output but does not mention cache read, and this test now locks the 5% figure in.
findings.failure_mode: If the vendor price for cache reads is $0.40, the cost ledger (LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH) and cost-budget-enforcer undercount cache-read spend on the default `opus` alias by 2x, and the test prevents a later correction from landing without a test edit.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-check the cache_read_per_mtok value for claude-opus-5-5 against the vendor pricing page and the ratio used by the other Anthropic entries in model-config.yaml. If the vendor figure is $0.40, update both the catalog entry and the RES-1 expectation to 400000.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff-touched allowlist test documents that cycle-126 dropped gemini-2.5-pro from the literal VALID_FLATLINE_MODELS list and now only asserts it is admitted by the forward-compat regex. The diff-touched RES-4 and RES-6 residue checks grep alternative-model.md but do not cover gemini-2.5-pro, so the persona's 'Operator extension' example continues to recommend it.
findings.description: alternative-model.md still tells operators they MAY swap the tertiary panelist to `gemini-2.5-pro`. The allowlist test in this diff was rewritten because that id is no longer in the literal allowlist, and validate_model now accepts it only via the forward-compat pattern. If the catalog no longer serves gemini-2.5-pro (the generated allowlist is derived from the catalog), an operator following the persona doc passes validation but fails at resolution/invoke time. The residue grep in RES-6 does not include this id, so the stale example is not caught by the new acceptance tests.
findings.failure_mode: Operator configures the L1 panel tertiary as gemini-2.5-pro per the persona doc; validate_model passes; the hop fails later with an unknown-model error from model-invoke, after validation has already reported the config as sound.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm whether gemini-2.5-pro is still a served catalog id. If not, change the persona example to a served alias (e.g. `gemini-3.1-pro`) and extend the RES-6 regex to cover `gemini-2\.5-pro` under .claude/data so the doc cannot drift again.

findings.description: The diff attributes two hunks at lines 191-217 to .claude/data/personas/alternative-model.md, and their content is a bats test (`@test "T5 — operator override at tier_groups.mappings wins..."`) that invokes `$RESOLVER resolve ...` and parses JSON. The P0 full-file context supplied for the same path is a roughly 35-line persona markdown with no bats content and no line 191. One of the two is wrong: either the T5 hunk belongs to a resolver bats file and the diff path is mislabeled, or the persona document that gets loaded as a panelist prompt carries embedded shell test code.
findings.failure_mode: If the hunk really lives in the persona file, a bats test body is injected into every alternative-model panelist prompt and RES-4/RES-6 greps over .claude/data will scan test fixtures as if they were persona text. If the path is mislabeled, the T5 expectation change (claude-sonnet-4-6 to claude-sonnet-5) was reviewed against the wrong file and its real location was not covered by this review.
findings.suggested_fix: Verify with `git show <commit> --stat` which file actually contains the T5 test. If it is the persona file, move the test to tests/unit and keep the persona document prose-only. If it is mislabeled, re-run the review bundle against the correct path.
